content: 1. The preferred regimen for treating infective endocarditis includes either Penicillin G at a dose of 24 million units per 24 hours administered intravenously, either continuously or in divided doses every 4 to 6 hours for a duration of 6 weeks, or Ceftriaxone at a dose of 2 grams per 24 hours administered intravenously or intramuscularly in a single daily dose for 6 weeks. This should be combined with Gentamicin at a dose of 3 mg/kg per 24 hours administered intravenously or intramuscularly in a single daily dose for 2 weeks. 2. An alternative preferred regimen involves Vancomycin at a dose of 30 mg/kg per 24 hours administered intravenously in divided doses every 12 hours, not exceeding a total of 2 grams per 24 hours, for a duration of 6 weeks. 3. For pediatric patients, the recommended doses are as follows: Penicillin G at 200,000 units/kg per 24 hours administered intravenously in divided doses every 4 to 6 hours; Ceftriaxone at 100 mg/kg per 24 hours administered intravenously or intramuscularly in a single daily dose; Gentamicin at 3 mg/kg per 24 hours administered intravenously or intramuscularly in a single daily dose or divided every 8 hours; and Vancomycin at 40 mg/kg per 24 hours administered intravenously in divided doses every 8 to 12 hours. 4. For dental procedures requiring antibiotic prophylaxis, the preferred oral regimen is a single dose of Amoxicillin 2 grams taken 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. For pediatric patients, the dose is Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg as a single dose 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. 5. If oral medication cannot be taken, the preferred regimen includes Ampicillin 2 grams intramuscularly or intravenously as a single dose 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure, or Cefazolin 1 gram intramuscularly or intravenously, or Ceftriaxone 1 gram intramuscularly or intravenously, all as single doses 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. For pediatric patients, the doses are Ampicillin 50 mg/kg, Cefazolin 50 mg/kg, or Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg. 6. For patients allergic to penicillins or ampicillin, the preferred oral regimen includes Cephalexin 2 grams, Clindamycin 600 mg, Azithromycin 500 mg, or Clarithromycin 500 mg, all as single doses taken 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. For pediatric patients, the doses are Cephalexin 50 mg/kg, Clindamycin 20 mg/kg, and Azithromycin or Clarithromycin 15 mg/kg. 7. For patients allergic to penicillins or ampicillin and unable to take oral medication, the preferred regimen includes Cefazolin 1 gram or Ceftriaxone 1 gram intramuscularly or intravenously, or Clindamycin 600 mg intramuscularly or intravenously, all as single doses 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. For pediatric patients, the doses are Cefazolin 50 mg/kg intramuscularly or intravenously, Ceftriaxone 20 mg/kg intramuscularly or intravenously, or Clindamycin 20 mg/kg intramuscularly or intravenously. 8. Antibiotic prophylaxis solely to prevent infective endocarditis is no longer recommended for patients undergoing gastrointestinal or genitourinary tract procedures. 9. For respiratory tract procedures, the preferred oral regimen is a single dose of Amoxicillin 2 grams taken 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. For pediatric patients, the dose is Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg as a single dose 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. 10. If oral medication cannot be taken for respiratory tract procedures, the preferred regimen includes Ampicillin 2 grams intramuscularly or intravenously, Cefazolin 1 gram intramuscularly or intravenously, or Ceftriaxone 1 gram intramuscularly or intravenously, all as single doses 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. For pediatric patients, the doses are Ampicillin 50 mg/kg, Cefazolin 50 mg/kg, or Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg. 11. For patients allergic to penicillins or ampicillin undergoing respiratory tract procedures, the preferred oral regimen includes Cephalexin 2 grams, Clindamycin 600 mg, Azithromycin 500 mg, or Clarithromycin 500 mg, all as single doses taken 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. For pediatric patients, the doses are Cephalexin 50 mg/kg, Clindamycin 20 mg/kg, and Azithromycin or Clarithromycin 15 mg/kg. 12. For patients allergic to penicillins or ampicillin and unable to take oral medication for respiratory tract procedures, the preferred regimen includes Cefazolin 1 gram or Ceftriaxone 1 gram intramuscularly or intravenously, or Clindamycin 600 mg intramuscularly or intravenously, all as single doses 30 to 60 minutes before the procedure. For pediatric patients, the doses are Cefazolin 50 mg/kg intramuscularly or intravenously, Ceftriaxone 20 mg/kg intramuscularly or intravenously, or Clindamycin 20 mg/kg intramuscularly or intravenously. 13. For surgical procedures involving infected skin, skin structures, or musculoskeletal tissue, it is reasonable to include an agent active against staphylococci and beta-hemolytic streptococci, such as an antistaphylococcal penicillin or a cephalosporin, as part of the therapeutic regimen for treating the infection.
